title: Admin authorization threat remediation and SSO audit playbook
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: This ticket captures the remediation plan and verification steps for a set of security findings uncovered during the February 2025 internal security review and an external pen-test with focus areas in RBAC v2 role mapping, admin session elevation, SAML assertion handling, and audit log completeness. Scope includes code fixes, config hardening, audit pipeline changes, and rollout/playbook updates for on-call and SRE teams.

Background: During the latest pen-test we identified four classes of issues: 1) role-translation edge cases where legacy RBAC v1 policies could map to broader privileges under RBAC v2; 2) SAML assertion replay and binding validation gaps in our admin SSO flow (third-party IdP integrations); 3) inconsistent audit logging for elevated admin actions and cross-service requests (missing correlation IDs and incomplete request metadata); 4) an operational gap in emergency admin escalation that bypasses audit retention policy. The findings are documented in the pen-test report and linked artifacts below.

Goals:
- Close the RBAC mapping and policy-evaluation loopholes that allow unintended privilege expansion.
- Harden SAML assertion validation and make assertion telemetry visible in audit logs.
- Ensure all admin-sensitive actions are logged with a minimum retained schema (timestamp, actor, actor-method, role-at-time, request-id, service, outcome, source-ip).
- Validate fixes via unit tests, integration tests, fuzzing of policy translation, and a scoped red-team re-test.

High-level remediation plan:
1) RBAC v2 policy-eval fixes: add strict deny override rules and a compatibility shim that rejects ambiguous role bindings during migration. Implement deterministic conflict resolution and add regression tests for known failure modes.
2) SSO/SAML hardening: enforce signature and audience checks, reject assertions without one-time-use IDs, add nonce cache with TTL and drift tolerance, and tighten clock skew acceptance. Add automated conformance tests against our CI IdP test harness.
3) Audit pipeline: augment request path instrumentation to propagate a persistent correlation-id for admin workflows and require it to be returned by downstream services. Expand audit schema and add alerts for missing fields. Backfill missing critical events from the last 30 days into long-term cold storage for incident analysis.
4) Admin escalation playbook: update runbooks to include manual verification steps and temporary authorization tokens that are single-use, timeboxed, and fully logged. Create a verification checkbox in the Console for emergency role grants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration test coverage added for policy-eval edge cases and SAML validation rules.
- Pen-test follow-up confirms remediations (low/none severity regressions).
- Audit logs include required fields for 100% of admin operations over a 7-day sampling window.
- Console reflects emergency escalation controls and logs are queryable by Security and SRE.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Stricter SAML validation could break customers with misconfigured IdPs. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout, communicate with accounts owning Dedicated/Private deployments, and provide a compatibility-mode with telemetry and warnings.
- Risk: Audit schema change increases storage and cost. Mitigation: tiered retention and compress/backfill strategy; show cost impact estimates.
